links.outcome: Readability of chatbot responses on nocturnal enuresis (FRES, FKGL)
links.effect: All chatbots produced 'difficult to read' text (FRES 33.6-40.9), requiring university-level comprehension (FKGL 20.3-21.9), limiting accessibility for parents.
links.quote: All chatbots generated texts in the "difficult to read" range (FRES: 33.6-40.9), requiring university-level comprehension (FKGL: 20.3-21.9), thereby substantially limiting accessibility for the target parent audience.

links.outcome: Reading level of chatbot health information versus target parent audience
links.effect: FKGL 20.3-21.9 (university level) and FRES 33.6-40.9 across GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Pro and DeepSeek R1, far above appropriate lay reading level.
links.quote: All chatbots generated texts in the "difficult to read" range (FRES: 33.6-40.9), requiring university-level comprehension (FKGL: 20.3-21.9), thereby substantially limiting accessibility for the target parent audience.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of three LLMs (GPT-4o, Gemini, DeepSeek) answering frequently asked questions about nocturnal enuresis for patients/parents using readability metrics (FRES, FKGL) and validated quality tools (EQIP, mDISCERN).
